paragraphs: Markets over the last day: the eight tracked equity indices moved -0.06% on average, with FTSE 100 strongest (+0.99%) and Nikkei 225 weakest (-2.17%). Brent crude changed -1.14% to 105.43. Gold changed +0.63% to 4,217.0. Bitcoin changed -0.44% to 83,308.6406. The US 10-year yield stands at 5.24%, a relative move of -0.08%. Among the firms tracked, EQT (+2.93%) and Glencore (+2.80%) moved the most.

Deals and capital markets: Private equity puts string of UK high street names up for sale (FT Markets). Owners of PizzaExpress, Morrisons and Itsu seeking exits as buyout groups cool on sector Deals and capital markets: CVC sought to hush Israel defence deal to avoid controversy (FT Markets). Private equity firm made unusual decision not to announce its acquisition of a 40% stake in camouflage maker Fibrotex Geopolitics and trade: Pakistan’s hard choice on Saudi Arabia’s war in Yemen (FT World). Defence pacts and financial reliance on Riyadh give Islamabad little leeway to avoid Houthi conflict Geopolitics and trade: UK imposes new sanctions on Iran over RAF Fairford incident (FT World). Andy Burnham says events at Gloucestershire base used by US military were ‘almost certainly directed’ by Islamic Revolutionary Guards Also ranking highly: What a $30bn Aussie data centre IPO debacle actually means (FT Markets).
